meta.name: Three-VM node-ready
meta.description: Install Node.js 22.x on host, agent, and visitor VMs and point @lamalibre at the Feria dev registry.

sections.label: Install Node.js 22.x and configure Feria registry

steps.label: Install Node.js + Feria registry on host
steps.bash:
set -euo pipefail
if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "npm already available ($(npm --version))"
else
  apt-get update
  apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg
  curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | bash -
  apt-get install -y nodejs
fi
GATEWAY="$(ip route | awk '/default/{print $3; exit}')"
if [ -z "${GATEWAY}" ]; then GATEWAY="192.168.2.1"; fi
printf '@lamalibre:registry=http://%s:4873\n' "${GATEWAY}" | tee /root/.npmrc /home/ubuntu/.npmrc >/dev/null
# Every account on the VM (the panel's lamaste user, agent and app accounts)
# resolves @lamalibre through npm's global configuration too: a VM never asks
# npmjs or the hosted Feria for Lamaste's packages (spec 68 checks).
GLOBALRC="$(npm config get globalconfig)"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "${GLOBALRC}")"
{ grep -v '^@lamalibre:registry=' "${GLOBALRC}" 2>/dev/null || true; printf '@lamalibre:registry=http://%s:4873\n' "${GATEWAY}"; } > "${GLOBALRC}.tmp"
chmod 0644 "${GLOBALRC}.tmp" && mv "${GLOBALRC}.tmp" "${GLOBALRC}"

# The VMs share the Mac's VM bridge with their internal 10.13.37.x/10.13.39.x
# addresses. The Mac must never learn one of those (multipass finds a VM's
# address by its MAC in the Mac's ARP table, and an internal one there makes
# every `multipass exec` time out after a restart): answer an ARP request only
# from the same subnet, and name in a request only the address of the target's.
printf 'net.ipv4.conf.all.arp_ignore = 2\nnet.ipv4.conf.all.arp_announce = 2\nnet.ipv4.conf.default.arp_ignore = 2\nnet.ipv4.conf.default.arp_announce = 2\n' > /etc/sysctl.d/60-rodeo-arp.conf
sysctl -q --load=/etc/sysctl.d/60-rodeo-arp.conf
